riassunto.titolo_giorno: Claude entra nelle riunioni e Meta Muse sbarca sugli smartwatch
riassunto.in_breve: Claude si prepara a partecipare direttamente alle riunioni di lavoro per svolgere compiti operativi in tempo reale, mentre Meta Muse porta l'assistente al polso tramite orologi intelligenti. Questi sviluppi mostrano come l'AI stia uscendo dalle finestre di chat tradizionali per integrarsi nelle conversazioni vocali e nei dispositivi di tutti i giorni.

da_provare.a_cosa_serve: Consente a chiunque in azienda o in uno studio di modificare testi e contenuti di un sito web personalizzato senza toccare il codice di programmazione.
da_provare.come_sfruttarla: Aggiornare rapidamente le informazioni di una pagina web senza dover attendere l'intervento dello sviluppatore.

da_provare.a_cosa_serve: Genera preventivi automatici tramite AI per officine meccaniche e laboratori specializzati in lavorazioni CNC e carpenteria di lamiere.
da_provare.come_sfruttarla: Velocizzare il calcolo dei prezzi e l'invio delle offerte commerciali ai clienti di lavorazioni su misura.

da_provare.a_cosa_serve: Funge da bot alternativo a Grok, funzionando con i propri modelli AI preferiti a costo zero per gestire conversazioni automatiche.
da_provare.come_sfruttarla: Automatizzare interazioni e risposte online collegando il modello di intelligenza artificiale desiderato.

da_provare.a_cosa_serve: Assistente virtuale pensato per essere aggiunto alle chat di gruppo della famiglia per coordinare attività e rispondere alle richieste pratiche di casa.
da_provare.come_sfruttarla: Tenere traccia degli impegni familiari direttamente all'interno delle conversazioni condivise.

osint.a_cosa_serve: Repertorio di fonti informative, database e registri pubblici per effettuare verifiche e indagini a fonti aperte su realtà e soggetti in Thailandia.
osint.come_sfruttarla: Verificare informazioni su fornitori o soggetti esteri attraverso i portali ufficiali e i registri aperti locali.

gemme.a_cosa_serve: Una mappa interattiva della città di Valencia ricreata interamente in pixel art isometrica, esplorabile liberamente dal centro storico fino alla spiaggia.
gemme.perche_gemma: Gratuita, senza annunci e basata su dati geografici 3D aperti, ridipinti tessera per tessera da un modello visivo.
gemme.con_ai: Mostra come utilizzare modelli generativi visivi per trasformare dati geografici aperti in un'interfaccia a mappa navigabile.

gemme.a_cosa_serve: Sistema privato e autonomo per archiviare e gestire la propria raccolta di foto e video su un server o computer di casa, in alternativa ai servizi cloud.
gemme.perche_gemma: Open source e focalizzata sulla privacy: con la versione 3.4.0 introduce il supporto per le immagini JPEG XL e la gestione dei tag direttamente da smartphone.
gemme.con_ai: Consente di applicare modelli visivi locali sul proprio server per indicizzare volti, oggetti e luoghi senza inviare le proprie immagini all'esterno.

a59.titolo: Valencia, Spain in Sim City/Isometric View
a59.testo: An isometric pixel-art map of València, painted block by block. Zoom from the Micalet to the beach. An isometric pixel-art map of València, in the spirit of SimCity and of Isometric NYC . Every building is a real one, drawn from above at the same angle, block by block. The whole municipal term is painted, from the huerta to the Albufera, except a few small huerta exclaves where there's no 3D imagery to paint from. Real 3D city data is rendered from a fixed isometric camera. An image model trained on a hand-picked pixel-art style then repaints it, tile by tile, each tile continuing its painted neighbours so the city stays seamless. The sea, the port basins and the Albufera are drawn in the same style. Tiny València is free and has no ads. Painting it takes rented GPUs, and keeping it online a server. If you enjoy it, you can support it on Patreon. Buildings © Dirección General del Catastro · Aerial photo & terrain © IGN (PNOA, MDT05), CC BY 4.0 · Roads, boundary, coast & search © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL · 3D reference: Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles via Cesium ion.

a138.titolo: Adobe is going all in on agentic AI
a138.testo: Adobe is committing itself to the notion that chatbots and AI agents could be your next design assistant, or even automate creative workflows and repetitive tasks on your behalf. Some of the tools and features announced today at Adobe’s Max conference in Miami, Florida, include allowing your preferred third-party AI agents to access and change Creative Cloud projects, new capabilities for Adobe’s Firefly AI Assistant, and the ability for AI agents to keep perpetually running recurring work in the background. Adobe is going all in on agentic AI Third-party AI agents can use Creative Cloud apps for you, and Firefly’s AI Assistant can run your social media accounts. Local Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations for Creative Cloud tools were previewed at the event, which aim to give you a choice between using Adobe’s own AI assistants, or the third-party agents you already use everyday. The integrations enable external AI agents from providers like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic to work locally in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects, where they can make direct changes to native project files on your computer. You can take over from the agents at any time to manually refine the work because all layers, vectors, bins, and sequences remain editable. Agents that are connected to other MCP-capable tools can also include them in the same workflow, such as asking the AI agent to pull reference documents from Google Docs, design a project around them in Adobe’s tools, and then share the results with colleagues or clients in Slack. Creative Cloud local MCP integrations aren’t available yet, but Adobe says a private beta will be launching in early 2027. “Always-on” agents were also previewed at Adobe’s Max event, which can perform recurring tasks continuously in the…

a148.titolo: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS
a148.testo: Meta is bringing its Muse AI agent to the Apple Watch and Android’s Wear OS, the company announced on Monday. With the launch, users can now interact with Meta’s AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation directly on their smartwatch. The smartwatch launch comes just a month after Meta introduced a dedicated iPad app for Muse. First launched on the App Store in September, the AI assistant’s expansion across Apple devices signals Meta’s growing ambitions for its consumer AI product and its focus on making Muse a central part of its ecosystem. Muse is now one of dozens of consumer-facing AI agents competing for users’ attention. Like many of its competitors, it allows users to connect their accounts to manage email, meetings, bills, and more, while also handling tasks such as booking reservations, ordering groceries, setting goals, and making purchases. Users can also personalize their Muse avatar to their liking and change it into something that resembles a person, an animal, or another type of character. Despite being a relatively new product, Meta has wasted little time introducing new capabilities to Muse. A few days ago, Meta launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with Muse. Spaces function as dedicated conversations around specific topics, which Meta describes as “custom experiences” as they’re mini apps that are built on the fly. They appear in the sidebar of the Muse interface and bring up a focused conversation where the AI agent works toward a particular goal on the user’s behalf. Last week, Meta rolled out the ability for users in the U.S. to video chat with their Muse AI avatar. a149.titolo: Adobe brings AI agents and new creative tools to Photoshop, Premiere, and Firefly
a149.testo: Adobe is pouring more AI into its products, including Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, and InDesign, in a major product feature announcement at its MAX event in Miami. The company is also expanding AI capabilities in its creative tool, Firefly, and releasing a Model Context Protocol (MCP) that lets other chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini use Adobe features. Adobe’s Firefly app is moving into Figma’s territory with a new prototyping tool in private beta called Builder, which lets users create designs to show off ideas. There is also a new tool to create on-brand graphs, along with an image-editing tool that lets you change part of an image without changing other objects. A new AI-powered video tool in Firefly will allow users to assemble a video from clips and other elements like images and sound effects. The company is making its agent proactive and always on so that it can get more context about work and be present for any action. Adobe is also making it easier for people to take quick action, like removing the background or generating a thumbnail for a video. The company has already added a ton of AI features across its apps like Photoshop, Express, Premiere, and Illustrator. At the MAX event, Adobe is continuing the trend. Photoshop is getting a new relighting feature and sliders for prompt-based generative styles; Premiere will have a new color grading system for professionals and an object removal feature for video; and Lightroom has a way to correct blinking eyes and a blemish removal tool. Adobe already offers a lot of third-party models from companies like Google, Runway, ElevenLabs, Black Forest Labs, OpenAI, Kling, and ByteDance. a152.titolo: Spotify’s AI DJ gets new voices, personalities, and an option for less chatter
a152.testo: Spotify’s AI DJ, one of the company’s earlier efforts in embracing AI technology to connect people with their favorite music, is getting an upgrade. On Tuesday, the streamer announced that users will now be able to customize their DJ more like they can an AI assistant, by choosing between different voices and personalities. Those who like the feature, but not all the chatter, can also now opt for an experience with less commentary in between sets. Since first launching the AI DJ in 2023, Spotify has leveraged AI to improve all areas of its app. Most recently, that has included updates that allow users to chat with a conversational AI agent about music, fine-tune their recommendations with prompts, create playlists with AI, and work with third-party agents like ChatGPT and Claude. However, the DJ remains one of Spotify’s most popular AI features, as it’s used by over 94 million Spotify Premium listeners. Now, it’s revisiting one of its first major AI features, taking a cue from the personalization options other AI assistants routinely offer. With the update, Spotify Premium subscribers will be able to choose from an expanded set of AI DJ voices in both English and Spanish. The voices include seven English options with British, American, Irish, Australian, and Indian accents, and two new Spanish options. The different voices will have their own unique personalities as well. For instance, users can pick between three American voices, one of which is laid-back and warm (Casey), another that’s direct and has an edge (Tess), and a third that has a Southern accent and a youthful energy (Lane).
